# rmux 0.1.8 — preview
This release makes returning to a project more reliable and improves keyboard navigation, document previews, and the browser demo.
## Project workspaces
- Opening a project from VS Code now reuses its resolved folder path. Two projects named `api` get separate workspaces, and renaming a workspace no longer breaks reuse. - Existing terminals keep their processes, layout, and working directories. Project identity survives saved sessions and moves between windows; symlink aliases resolve to the same project. - Matching older workspaces are adopted when their name and original launch directory agree. Ambiguous matches are reported instead of guessed. - Workspace search results and sidebar tooltips show the project path. Sidebar shortcut hints follow your configured bindings.
See the [VS Code setup guide](../guide/vscode.md) for the single-setting setup.
## Keyboard navigation and previews
- Shell line-start, line-end, and delete-to-start actions can be found in the command palette and assigned shortcuts. - Shortcut configuration catches conflicting sequence prefixes in overlapping contexts. Keyboard Shortcuts also lists configured literal terminal-text bindings. - Markdown previews can follow local document and directory links. Document preview Back/Forward history retains search and display state, and replacing a preview preserves the original terminal focus target.
## Browser demo
- Edit sample commands with cursor movement, word navigation, Home/End, and deletion, including Unicode text and narrow panes. - Recall previous sample commands with Up/Down or Ctrl+P/N, then return to your unfinished draft. History is bounded and separate for each session.
## Availability and checks
GitHub builds the macOS Apple Silicon DMG and ZIP, Linux x86-64 tarball, and Windows x86-64 ZIP. macOS is signed and notarized, with Sparkle updates.
Focused checks cover shortcut conflicts, preview loading/history, sample command editing/history, and project identity. A native smoke check confirmed that reopening and renaming projects retains the same terminal process. Browser editing and workspace switching were reviewed; the latest history addition and native visual changes still need a visual pass. Cross-Space focus remains unverified, and native Windows runtime validation remains deferred. The browser demo uses sample sessions, not real shells.
